## About

**360Pano3D** is an open-source, self-hostable workflow that turns raw scan data into a
walkable 3D forest twin in the browser. Six fisheye photos are stitched into an
equirectangular panorama (Hugin) and served through a Pannellum viewer; terrestrial laser
scans (E57) are converted into RGB point clouds and streamed as Potree octrees. A processing
step derives individual-tree inventory markers (position, height, DBH proxy) directly from
the point cloud and overlays them on both the panorama and the 3D view, so photographic and
structural data stay linked to the same scan positions.

The demo below is a static export of the gallery: a Renon TLS scene (Italian Alps, evergreen
spruce stand) with 87 automatically derived tree markers and a full point cloud, plus a
fisheye panorama scene from Hechingen. Upload and processing of new scenes run on the
self-hosted stack (Caddy + Garage object storage + FastAPI), which isn't part of this static
demo.
